items.title: Chester Zardis Interview, 1966-03-09
items.q: So I wanted to learn to fiddle after this man, Billy Marrera, can play so much fiddle. I said, well I'm going to have to learn. So when I asked him and he said yes, he said I could learn, he said I think you'd make a good musician.

ctx.x: Yeah Buddy could spell. But he was fine boy though. I was going to ask you again about your very early life, which you didn't tell so much about when you were going over that material. You were born 1900 you say? That's right. Can you tell us anything about your parents? Did they play any instrument?

No, I'll tell you what, when I told you before like Billy went to summon that bass for five dollars, I told my mother I was going to buy that bass. Did she sing or play piano? My mama? No. My mother didn't want me to play. No fiddle at all, no kind of music. She said, the musicians was no good. You understand? Because the women runs behind musicians too much. Who was your cousin? Did he ever work as a musician?
